messages.subject_clean: Accounting for covariates on tile analyses
messages.body_plain:
dear all

im working with RRBS data from pig. first i did a tile analyses bust since in each treatments i have different animals with different ages, i want to correct the model for both biological differences and age differences. i realized that if i include both age and animal, i would end up with too many covariates/ too few replicates. therefore for now i just considered animals as covariates. although i did tile analysis but dataSim function is giving me base resolution result. any idea how to Accounting for covariates on tile? here is my command line

> library(methylKit)

> mylist=list("Fenris-1-391.sorted.sam", "Norden-1-738623.sorted.sam", "Fenris-27-395.sorted.sam", "Artist-18-393.sorted.sam")

> my.methRaw=processBismarkAln(location = mylist, sample.id <http://sample.id> = list("ctrl1","ctrl2","test1","test2"),assembly="Sscrofa11.1", read.context="CpG",nolap = FALSE,mincov = 10,minqual = 20,phred64 = FALSE,treatment = c(0,0,1,1))

> filtered.myobj=filterByCoverage(my.methRaw,lo.count = 10,lo.perc = NULL,hi.count = NULL,hi.perc = 99.9)

> normalized.myobj=normalizeCoverage(filtered.myobj)

> meth=unite(normalized.myobj, destrand=FALSE)

> tiles=tileMethylCounts(meth, win.size = 300, step.size = 300, cov.bases = 4)

> covariates=data.frame(animal=c(1,2,1,3))

> new=dataSim(replicates = 4, sites = 20000, treatment = c(0,0,1,1))

> diffmeth=calculateDiffMeth(new, covariates = covariates)

although i did tile analysis first but dataSim function is giving me base resolution result. any idea how to Accounting for covariates on tile?

> view(diffmeth)

chr1               10            11             +          2.5e-08           1.55e-7       -40.5
...

furthermore i tried to set the site equal to tiles but it in not working for me ! any help is greatly appreciated.

> new2=dataSim(replicates = 4, sites = tiles, treatment = c(0,0,1,1))

Error in matrix(ncol = replicates * 3, nrow = sites) :
  non-numeric matrix extent

thanks alot

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
our tests checks if there is an association between eigenvectors and the potential batch effects. In our case, we obtain eigenvectors from scaled CpGs X samples matrix, where CpGs are on the rows and samples are on the columns. In this case, eigenvectors can be interpreted as CpG methylation patterns across samples (without the correct scale). We check either with cor.test() (if batch effects are numeric such as age) or wilcox.test (if batch effects are categorical, factor variables) to check the association between eigenvectors and batch effects.

You can probably test the association between eigenvectors and batch effects with linear models to check combinations of batch effects rather than testing one by one, but I think the main difference is the way you apply PCA, that is different than what we do and I'm not sure how to interpret what you are doing.

Best,
Altuna

messages.body_plain:
We carried out RRBS with the Diagenode kit. We ran SE 50bp sequencing and used Trim Galore ( --rrbs and —non_directional) and Bismark prior Methylkit. We have identified CpG DMSs between two groups of 6 samples using the overdispersion chi2 method. We have also used destrand=TRUE setting. At the end we realized that more than 10% of our DMSs are at 50 bp physical distance from each other. When switching the destrand to FALSE the number of DMS was divided by 2 and the 50bp distance peak at the DMS distance distribution disappeared.
1/ What is the reason of our observation? Is this a complete artefact?
2/ Do we have to use therefore the destrand=FALSE setting or can we extract some real positives from the TRUE analysis what we wouldn’t identify with the FALSE?

Thanks for your help,
Tamas
